title: A product repair can be followed by an official finding that the repair was ineffective
source_unit: CPSC Sauna360 Tylö Halmstad and Kiruna Hybrid sauna recall and September 2026 expansion
geography: United States; Sauna360 Tylö Halmstad and Kiruna Hybrid sauna rooms

observations.period: October 23, 2025; first CPSC recall and free professional repair route

denominator.unit: sauna rooms covered by the notice; not unique owners or households

hazard.value: Bench seating could break and create a fall hazard; CPSC reported seven breakage reports, including one head-and-neck injury

first_remedy.value: Sauna360 offered additional hardware, a revised manual, and free professional repair

owner_response.unit: missing owner notice, possession, appointment, repair completion, downtime, safe use, substitute access, and later outcome

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official CPSC October 2025 recall notice; product-level hazard and offered remedy are kept separate from purchaser-level notice, repair receipt, and safe restoration.
observations.uncertainty: Reported units and incidents are notice-level counts, not unique-owner rates or exposure estimates. The public record does not identify which owners received notice, needed repair, or completed it.
observations.subgroup: Sauna360 Tylö Halmstad and Kiruna Hybrid sauna rooms covered by the recall; no owner-level subgroup is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A repair offer and incident report do not establish that every listed owner was exposed or that the remedy was completed and effective.

observations.period: September 17, 2026; CPSC expansion after reported ineffectiveness of the earlier repair

denominator.unit: sauna rooms covered by the expanded notice, including products covered by the earlier recall; not a unique-owner denominator

remedy_durability.value: The expansion states that the previous repair was ineffective and reports 77 additional breakage reports, including six injuries

second_remedy.value: Owners were instructed to stop using the product even if they received the 2025 remedy and were offered another free professional retrofit with additional hardware

second_repair_receipt.unit: missing first-repair receipt, second-notice receipt, appointment, second-repair completion, downtime, substitute access, residual loss, and later trust or behavior

mechanism.value: A first repair offer or even reported repair implementation does not establish durable safety when a later official expansion says the repair was ineffective; remedy durability becomes a separate control surface

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official CPSC September 2026 recall expansion; the later correction is treated as a product-level institutional finding, not as evidence that every first repair failed.
observations.uncertainty: The expansion does not identify repaired units among the reported incidents, owner-level notice or appointment, failure mechanism by product, or completed second repair. Unit and incident counts remain notice-level figures.
observations.subgroup: Sauna360 sauna rooms covered by the expanded recall and any earlier-recall units; no owner, installer, or household outcome sample is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A repeat recall demonstrates institutional remedy failure at the product or system level without proving identical failure for every owner or predicting the second remedy's outcome.

boundary: This record establishes a product-level hazard, first repair, reported remedy ineffectiveness, and second repair route. It does not estimate purchaser exposure, notice, repair completion, safe restoration, trust, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the two official CPSC recall notices; owner files, raw complaints, direct identifiers, and installer records are not retained.
